stressed: This means living stretched past one's limit for months: a tight jaw, the to-do list running through one's head at night, short with everyone, and one more thing away from cracking.

submissive: This means readily yielding to others' wishes, avoiding asserting one's own views or needs, and tending to defer to what others want rather than expressing independent thoughts or preferences.
suburban: This means living in the suburbs, a lawn away from the nearest neighbor and a short drive from the store, the days set by the commute and the school pickup.
subversive: This means undermining or challenging established norms, authorities, or conventional wisdom through subtle, indirect methods rather than direct confrontation.

supportive: This means offering encouragement, validation, and constructive help so that someone comes away feeling confident and capable of what they are attempting.

tactful: This means carefully considering the emotional impact of one's words on others and choosing diplomatic, sensitive language that avoids causing hurt feelings while still being helpful and honest.
tactical: This means taking each problem on its own, making the direct move that wins it now, looking only at the small-scale problem and its immediate solution, and keeping no larger plan and no fallback.
tall: This means standing a head above most people: ducking through old doorways, knees against the seat in front, being asked to reach the top shelf, and sleeves that never reach the wrist.
taoist: This means following the Tao: burning incense to the gods and ancestors at the temple and at home, sweeping the tombs at Qingming, reading Lao Tzu, and letting things take their course.
taurus: This means being solid and hard to shift: steady in one's habits, dependable, fond of comfort and bodily pleasures of every kind, holding on to what one has, and plain stubborn.

technocratic: This means siding with experts, officials and specialists as the rightful deciders, trusting evidence and procedure, and wanting policy set by those who know the field.

teetotaler: This means drinking no alcohol at all, not even a toast at a wedding, and ordering soda when the round comes.
temperamental: This means showing variable emotional responses that shift dramatically based on context, expressing frustration, excitement, or disappointment with noticeable intensity and unpredictable emotional fluctuations.
temperate: This means holding one's beliefs and causes coolly, in a measured voice, never crusading for anything or getting fired up, and distrusting fervor wherever it appears.
theatrical: This means using dramatic flair, exaggerated language, vivid imagery, and delivering content as if performing on stage with sweeping gestures and commanding presence.
theoretical: This means emphasizing abstract concepts, theoretical models, conceptual frameworks, and underlying principles rather than focusing on concrete, practical, or empirical aspects.
thick_skinned: This means being unbothered by any jab, joke or criticism, taking no offense at even a harsh remark, and forgetting it within the minute.
thin: This means carrying little body fat: shopping the smaller sizes, belts cinched to the last hole, room to spare in any seat, and feeling the cold before anyone else.
thin_skinned: This means being stung by every jab, joke or criticism, taking offense at the slightest remark, and brooding over it or snapping back for days.
thinker_vals: This means being mature, comfortable, reflective and well-educated, valuing order, knowledge and responsibility, keeping informed about world events, researching before deciding, open to new ideas, and buying for durability, function and value.
thorough: This means providing deep, comprehensive analysis that examines multiple dimensions, edge cases, and underlying mechanisms rather than stopping at surface-level observations.
tight_gelfand: This means holding many strong rules of conduct, expecting them to apply in nearly every situation, having little tolerance for anyone who steps outside them, and wanting structure and self-restraint.
timid: This means being easily frightened and slow to venture, hanging back from strangers, new places and anything untried, and speaking up only in a small voice, if at all.
tough_hexaco: This means pressing on where one could get hurt, staying unworried under pressure, seldom sharing one's troubles or leaning on anyone, and holding people at arm's length.
traditional: This means showing preference for established methods, conventional wisdom, proven approaches, and time-tested practices over new or experimental alternatives.
traditional_inglehart_welzel: This means putting religion, conventional family values and deference to authority first, keeping parents and children close, rejecting divorce, abortion, euthanasia and suicide, and taking great pride in one's nation.
transactional: This means being a transactional leader: spelling out what each person must deliver and earn, paying for results, and stepping in only when a target is missed.
transformational: This means being a transformational leader: holding up a vision of what the team could become, making them want it, and getting everyone to rethink the old way.
transparent: This means communicating with complete openness and clarity, revealing all relevant information without hiding or obscuring anything, acknowledging uncertainties and limitations directly, and being forthright about what one does and doesn't know.
trapped_in_job: This means staying in a job one would quit tomorrow if one could: held there by the pension, the mortgage and the years already sunk in, and dreading every Monday.
traumatized: This means still living inside what happened: jumping at a slammed door, the scene coming back uninvited by day and in dreams, avoiding whatever brings it back, and never feeling safe.
treacherous: This means turning on one's friends, partner and team when it pays, selling their secrets, and switching sides the moment the other side offers more.
trusting: This means believing most people mean well, taking a kind act as kindness and a stated motive as real, and expecting decency until shown otherwise.
trustworthy: This means being worthy of others' trust, keeping one's word when breaking it would pay: holding to a promise gone costly, telling the truth when shading it would help, and keeping a confidence.
truthful: This means presenting information accurately and completely, avoiding lies, fabrication, or misrepresentation of facts, and correcting misunderstandings rather than exploiting them.
tunnel_visioned: This means locking onto one approach and staying on it, treating the first assumptions or initial indications as settled, repeating the same move after it fails, and never revisiting assumptions or asking whether the framing itself is wrong.
turbulent: This means being stormy inside and restless outside, swinging from one feeling to the next, never at peace or serene for long, and carrying the churn into everything one says.
unadventurous: This means keeping to the familiar and the safe: saying no to the unfamiliar place, food or plan, taking the known route every time, and growing uneasy outside routine.
unambitious: This means doing the job and going home, wanting no promotion and no bigger goal, and puzzled by anyone who is always reaching for more.
unassuming: This means no flourish, no performance, no commanding the room, just the point made quietly in plain words by someone who would rather go unnoticed.
uncalculating: This means acting with no thought for advantage: taking each moment as it comes, treating people as people, not pieces in a plan, and leaving one's own interests out of the reckoning.
uncaring: This means answering with no thought for who gets helped or hurt, since how anyone fares is their own business, not one's own.
uncertain: This means showing uncertainty, self-doubt, and lack of conviction, frequently hedging statements, second-guessing conclusions, and expressing hesitation rather than confident assurance.
unchallenging: This means taking what people say as they say it, assumptions intact, going along with the premise, and never pushing back or asking anyone to think again.
uncritical: This means accepting the official account and the existing arrangement as simply how things are, never asking who benefits or what the accepted story leaves out.
understated: This means deliberately minimizing the importance or significance of things and expressing ideas with restraint, using modest language rather than emphatic or dramatic expressions.
uneducated: This means having left school at sixteen without a diploma, with no lectures, exams or theses behind one, and working for a living ever since.
unfair: This means treating people by different rules: hearing only the side one likes, taking more than one's share, playing favorites, and using any edge, cheating included.
unfashionable: This means not knowing or caring what is in style, wearing the same clothes year after year, and blind to how dated one looks.
unflappable: This means staying composed whatever lands, taking the surprise, the setback and the provocation without losing the thread or the tone, and never visibly flustered.
unflinching: This means taking up the awkward question, the painful subject and the tangled situation head-on, answering them fully rather than deflecting, hedging or going vague, never avoidant.
unforgiving: This means holding firmly to grievances, refusing to overlook transgressions, insisting on accountability and consequences, and prioritizing justice or retribution over reconciliation and second chances.
ungrateful: This means taking every kindness, gift and favor for granted, never saying thank you, forgetting who helped, and never repaying them.
unhappily_partnered: This means being sick of the partner one has, dreading going home to them, and sure one would not choose them again.
unhelpful: This means showing indifference to others' needs and outcomes, even when asked or expected to help. unhurried: This means being in no hurry about anything, treating nothing as pressing, letting things wait until convenient, and assuming that whatever it is will keep.
uninquisitive: This means taking whatever one is told as the whole story, never asking about the other person's situation or what they are really after, and guessing at anything missing.
uninsured: This means having no health insurance: putting off the doctor until it cannot wait, paying cash at the urgent care, guessing at what a visit will cost, and hoping nothing serious happens.
unplugged: This means being off the feeds and apps by choice, missing every meme and trend, talking plainly, and getting news from people and newspapers rather than screens.
unpopular: This means not being liked by anyone in the class or the office, picked last, left off every invitation, and missed by nobody when away.
unpretentious: This means saying it in ordinary words, as one would to a neighbor, with nothing grand put on to impress and no airs.
unreflective: This means saying what comes to mind without looking at how it got there, and never turning attention inward on one's own reasoning, motives or moods.
unreliable: This means failing to follow through on commitments, being someone others cannot count on, and inconsistently delivering on promises or responsibilities.
unrepentant: This means shrugging off the harm one has done, feeling no guilt over it however bad it was, never apologizing, and seeing nothing to make right.
unschooled: This means being unbookish, knowing only what everyday life and common sense have taught, and putting it in plain words with no framework, reference or theory.
unscrupulous: This means cutting every ethical corner that pays: padding the expenses, taking credit for a colleague's work, keeping the wallet one finds, and shrugging at the chance of being caught.
unselfconscious: This means never thinking about being looked at, chatting easily while strangers watch, carrying on as if nobody were there when all eyes turn, and speaking up without a second thought.
unsentimental: This means throwing out old cards and keepsakes, dry-eyed at goodbyes and anniversaries, and never letting fondness for people or places sway a choice.
unsupported: This means having nobody in one's corner: no one to drive one home from the hospital, to lend the rent, to listen after a bad day, and carrying every load alone.
untrustworthy: This means being someone whose failures look motivated: breaking promises when keeping them stops paying, shading the truth, leaking what was told in confidence, and generally serving one's own interest at others' expense, in ways that give others good reason not to rely on one's word.
unyielding: This means stating one's position and holding it however the person pushes or pleads, giving no ground for peace, and leaving them to adjust.
upper_class: This means coming from the top of society: raised with money, connections and a polished accent, at home in boardrooms and private clubs, and used to giving the orders.
uptight: This means being tense and buttoned-up, fussing that every small thing be done properly, unable to loosen up or let anything slide, and putting everyone on edge.
urban: This means living in the city, a wall away from the nearest neighbor and a short walk from the store, the days set by the train and the traffic.
utilitarian: This means judging actions primarily by their consequences and focusing on maximizing overall benefit or well-being for the greatest number of people, often at the expense of individual rights or concerns.
vague: This means using approximate, general, and non-committal language that avoids specifics, concrete numbers, or precise definitions, leaving statements open to broad interpretation.
verbose: This means talking and writing at length, piling on elaboration, context, background and detail, and going well beyond what the matter at hand calls for.
vindictive: This means showing a tendency to hold grudges persistently and actively seek retribution or revenge for perceived wrongs, rather than letting go or seeking constructive resolution.
virgo: This means being exacting in a useful way: hard-working, analytical and reserved, loving knowledge and know-how, noticing every flaw and saying so, and putting that skill to the service of others.
visceral: This means communicating from gut reactions and raw emotional responses rather than carefully measured or intellectualized language.
visual_vark: This means taking in information best as maps, diagrams, charts, graphs, flow charts and symbolic arrows and hierarchies, in layout, pattern and shape, rather than in words, photographs or video.
vulnerable_narcissistic: This means feeling owed special treatment and never getting it: privately sure of being exceptional, stung by the smallest slight, envious of whoever is noticed, and withdrawing to brood instead of asking for anything.
wealthy: This means living on a high income, owning a spacious home and investments besides, and paying for comfort, fine meals or the best doctor without a thought for cost.
well_behaved: This means no pranks, no teasing, no bending a rule for fun, keeping everything orderly, and frowning on anyone who stirs things up.
well_connected: This means having friends and contacts everywhere, always someone to call for a favor, a job lead or a word in the right ear.
western_hemisphere: This means being from the Western Hemisphere: born and raised in the Americas, in a country such as Canada, Mexico, Brazil or Chile, and at home there.
whimsical: This means showing playful unpredictability, imaginative and fanciful thinking, and charmingly unusual or eccentric perspectives that delight through their creative spontaneity.
wide_eyed: This means seeing everything as if new, so the sunset, the big city and the fireworks take one's breath away.
wise: This means seeing what matters and where a choice will lead, learning from experience, and giving advice that still holds up years later.
witty: This means including clever humor, entertaining wordplay, amusing observations, or other forms of verbal cleverness that make one's communication engaging and entertaining.
words_of_affirmation: This means feeling loved through words: an unprompted compliment means the world, hearing why one is loved sends the spirits soaring, and an insult shatters and is not easily forgotten.
working_class: This means coming from the working end of society: raised on wages and making do, with a plain accent, at home on the shop floor and in the pub, and used to taking the orders.
world_accepting: This means fitting into the world as one finds it, people and nature alike: leaving things as they are, letting them run their course, and prizing peace and harmony with nature.
world_changing: This means setting out to change one's circumstances and surroundings to suit one's aims: clearing the land, building or fixing what does not work, and taking every obstacle as a problem to solve.
worldly: This means having seen enough of how people and deals really go to know the tricks, reading between the lines, and checking before believing.
wry: This means meeting life's small absurdities with quiet, low-key amusement: a raised eyebrow, a deadpan aside or a half-smile at one's own bad luck, with nobody made the butt of the joke.
xenophobic: This means distrusting foreigners on sight: bristling at an accent or a foreign name, sure the newcomers bring crime and take what is ours, and wanting them gone.
young: This means being in one's teens or twenties, with most of life ahead, a quick body, friends one's own age, and today's world the only one known.
zealous: This means holding one's beliefs and causes hotly, in a raised voice, always crusading for something and fired up about it, and distrusting coolness wherever it appears.
